meta.note: Friday morning briefing. Three top stories: Carrier Q3 data-center orders +300%, backlog US$8.5 billion to a record; Trane backlog US$12.5 billion (+73%), Americas commercial HVAC orders +80%; Vertiv Q3 revenue +61%, orders doubled, completed US$1.45 billion UIG acquisition. Earnings season: JCI FY26 Q4 backlog US$23.0 billion to a record, Midea 9M net profit +9.3%, Gree Q3 net profit halved (copper/aluminum costs squeezed gross margin 5.62 pp). Tariffs: Busan Xi-Trump deal (China tariffs 57%->47%, rare-earth controls paused one year, reciprocal port fees halted; leaders announced, details pending); Section 338 Canada adjustment effective Oct 30 (some refrigeration equipment removed from the 50% list); Section 301 exclusions expire Nov 9, 10-day countdown. Second-round power-device hikes effective (onsemi Oct 10), INVT VSD price-adjustment letter effective Oct 8, MLCC lead times past 61 weeks, Kingboard's 8th CCL hike letter of the year, ethylene glycol +20.75%. Event library: 7 new events (Carrier Q3, Trane Q3, Gree Q3, INVT VSD, ethylene glycol, Busan deal, Vertiv SmartIT), 11 timeline appends (DRAM / MLCC / OSAT / CoolerMaster / CCL / Nexans / cloud capex / 338 / JCI / Samsung phones / Shenling convertible bond -> effective). Tier B batch 12: 1 hit (Coolants - ethylene glycol).

hotspot_events.title: Carrier Q3 data-center orders surge 300%, backlog tops US$8.5 billion to record high
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Measured +300% data-center cooling-source demand feeds directly into commercial chiller capacity and lead times
hotspot_events.summary: Carrier Q3 revenue US$6.26 billion (+12%, +15% organic), adjusted EPS US$0.87 (+30%); commercial HVAC orders +60%, data-center orders +300% (data-center sales ~2.5x last year, ~US$2.0 billion full-year target); backlog tops US$8.5 billion (+60%), a record; full-year revenue guidance raised to US$23.8-24.0 billion; tariff refunds also boosted profit.

hotspot_events.title: Trane Q3 revenue +18%, backlog jumps 73% to US$12.5 billion
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Americas commercial HVAC backlog +80%, applied-air lead times stay under pressure
hotspot_events.summary: Trane Q3 revenue US$6.76 billion (+18%, +16% organic), adjusted EPS US$4.86 (+25%); organic orders +20% (US$7.2 billion); total backlog US$12.5 billion (+73%, Americas commercial HVAC backlog +80%); full-year revenue growth guidance raised to ~13.5% (~11% organic); the earnings call also acknowledged supply-chain inflation pressure.

sources.outlet: Company 8-K filing (via TradingView) + Motley Fool earnings call transcript

hotspot_events.title: Vertiv Q3 revenue +61%, organic orders more than double, completes US$1.45 billion UIG acquisition
hotspot_events.heat_reason: AI data-center power-plus-cooling integration accelerates; OEM capacity scheduling and price-hike expectations heat up
hotspot_events.summary: Vertiv Q3 revenue US$4.31 billion (+61%), adjusted EPS US$2.21 (+78%), adjusted operating margin 25.2%, organic orders more than doubled YoY; full-year revenue guidance raised to US$14.45-14.85 billion; completed the ~US$1.45 billion all-cash acquisition of Utility Innovation Group on Oct 27 (up to US$1.15 billion in additional earnouts), doubling down on microgrid controls and behind-the-meter power architectures.

industry_updates.title: Johnson Controls FY26 Q4 beats expectations, backlog hits record US$23 billion
industry_updates.detail: FY26 Q4 (ended September 2026) released Oct 27: revenue US$7.11 billion (+10.4%, +12% organic), adjusted EPS US$1.66 (+31.7%), organic orders +44%, backlog US$23.0 billion (+43%) to a record, with data-center demand driving Americas applied HVAC orders; same day announced the sale of its global intrusion security business (DSC/Qolsys) to Truelink Capital (price undisclosed, expected to close H1 2027); initiated FY27 guidance (adjusted EPS US$6.15-6.30, organic revenue growth 11-12%).
industry_updates.source: JCI official PR Newswire earnings release (via Morningstar), 2026-10-27

industry_updates.title: Midea Q3 results: 9M net profit RMB 41.4 billion (+9.3%), Building Technologies the growth engine
industry_updates.detail: 9M revenue RMB 369.1 billion (+1.19%), net profit attributable to parent RMB 41.393 billion (+9.27%), Q3 net profit RMB 14.947 billion (+25.93%); Building Technologies revenue RMB 30.9 billion (+10%), robotics & automation RMB 24.9 billion (+10%), Q3 overseas OBM revenue +20%, RMB 13.3 billion in buybacks YTD.
industry_updates.source: China Securities Journal / cs.com.cn / The Paper (company filing basis), 2026-10-29

industry_updates.title: Gree Q3 results: Q3 net profit halved, worst Q3 report since listing
industry_updates.detail: Q3 revenue RMB 36.678 billion (-7.97%), net profit attributable to parent RMB 3.996 billion (-43.31%, largest Q3 single-quarter drop since listing); 9M revenue RMB 126.075 billion (-8.1%), net profit RMB 17.274 billion (-19.51%); Q3 copper and aluminum spot prices +35%/+15% YoY squeezed gross margin by 5.62 pp; ChinaIoL: 2026 9M China residential AC sell-through 150 million units (-8.4%), AVC projects Q4 industry sales -19.2%.

industry_updates.title: Shenling Environmental lands RMB 1.0 billion convertible bond, RMB 800 million for liquid-cooling smart manufacturing base
industry_updates.detail: Oct 26 issuance results disclosed: RMB 1.0 billion convertible bond placed, RMB 800 million for a liquid-cooling new-quality intelligent manufacturing base in Shunde, Foshan (land, filings and EIA all secured), RMB 200 million to replenish working capital; the company says growing liquid-cooling thermal-control orders have pushed existing capacity toward saturation.

industry_updates.title: Envicool Q3 results: revenue up, profit flat trend continues
industry_updates.detail: Q3 revenue RMB 1.933 billion (+33.04%), net profit RMB 184 million (+0.25%); 9M revenue RMB 4.95 billion (+22.94%), net profit RMB 369 million (-7.62%), mainly due to regional sales-mix changes, higher expenses and FX losses; operating cash flow RMB 214 million (+167%).

industry_updates.title: Vertiv launches SmartIT pre-engineered AI infrastructure platform (NVL72 liquid cooling)
industry_updates.detail: Released on the official site Oct 26: built on NVIDIA MGX and OCP ORV3 architecture, supporting GB300 NVL72, Vera Rubin NVL72 and DGX/HGX Rubin NVL8; integrates racks, DC power conversion & distribution, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, in-row cooling distribution and monitoring, factory pre-validated, now orderable globally; Oct 29 announced a global AI thermal-management and fluid-management ecosystem with Dow (advanced coolants) and Solenis (chemical water treatment).

siphon_effects.detail: TrendForce outlook: Q4 conventional DRAM contract prices +10%-15% QoQ, NAND +15%-20%; Samsung Oct 29 earnings call: Q3 DRAM ASP +20% QoQ, HBM4 shipments more than tripled QoQ, 2027 HBM capacity fully sold out, tightness continues; SK Hynix Oct 28 call: Q3 DRAM ASP +high-20% QoQ, DDR4 8Gb ~US$26 (~US$6.3 a year ago, ~4x), shortage expected through 2030.
siphon_effects.source: TrendForce / Pandromeda, Samsung Q3 earnings call, SK Hynix Q3 call, 2026-10-28/29

siphon_effects.detail: Samsung Electro-Mechanics MLCC lead times stretched to 52 weeks (Korean media, Oct 20), Q4 consumer X5R +25%-30%; Yageo plans another round late Oct-Nov (high-cap +50%, mid/low-cap +10%-30%), Sanhuan +10%-30% to distributors from October; TrendForce Oct 29: AI-grade MLCC shortage extends into H1 2027, Murata new capacity unlikely before 2028, Japanese MLCC makers highly likely to follow in November price talks; Murata issued EOL on select part numbers in 9 series in Sep-Oct (last order 2028-3-31).
siphon_effects.source: Korea Economic Daily (via Cailian Press) / 21st Century Business Herald, TrendForce Oct 29, 2026-10-20/22/29

siphon_effects.detail: Amazon Oct 29 earnings: Q3 capex US$77.3 billion (well above US$57.5 billion consensus), ~US$220 billion for full-year 2026, CEO guides 2027 "significantly higher"; AWS revenue US$46.0 billion (+39%), backlog US$578 billion, AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

Nexans CFO (Reuters, Oct 22): global cable capacity tight, building a new XLPE line takes ~3 years, France's Enedis has shifted procurement contracts from 1-year to 6-7 years to lock in supply; Oracle declared force majeure in September on a large New Mexico data-center project (insufficient power); ABB data-center orders up triple digits. High-speed fiber connectors (CCS / Amphenol) ~50-week lead times (hyperscalers locked in capacity years ahead).

Kingboard Laminates issued its 8th price-hike letter of the year on Oct 13 (2116 and thinner styles / PP +15%); Shengyi Technology raised boards/PP another 10%-20% in early October; electronic cloth 7628 up to RMB 13.5-14/m (~RMB 3.9 in Sep 2025, +200%+), lead times 12-18 months; 6-micron lithium-battery copper foil tolling rose from RMB 20,500 to 24,000/ton between Jul 20 and Oct 12 (+17.1%); Kingboard HTE copper foil tolling ~RMB 30,000/ton (~RMB 15,000 a year ago), inventory near zero (UBS, Oct 12).
siphon_effects.source: China Securities Journal, Securities Star (citing Mysteel / UBS), 2026-10-19/21

siphon_effects.detail: TrendForce (Oct 20): TSMC CoWoS monthly capacity 120-140K wafers, 2026 advanced-packaging capacity still 10%-20% short; Taiwan OSATs quoting +10%-30% for Q4 (EEWorld, Oct 17); ASE 2026 capex US$8.5 billion (+60%).

cross_industry.detail: Industrial-control components repriced across the board: Omron / Schneider relays +10%-25%, Turck / Pepperl+Fuchs sensors +15%-35%, Phoenix Contact / Weidmueller connectors +12%-30%, automation-line costs up ~8%-15% overall; some European chip lead times exceed 52 weeks, one major analog vendor advises customers to book orders into 2028.

TSMC 3nm +15% in 2026H2, another +5-10% in 2027, 2nm wafer ~US$30,000; 12/16/28nm potentially +10%; global 8-inch fab utilization ~90% on average; PSMC logic +10%-15%, memory foundry +45%; Intel (effective Sep 1) and Qualcomm Snapdragon X/X2 (effective Oct 1, +10%) have passed through price hikes.

Counterpoint preliminary (via Korea JoongAng Daily, Oct 15): Q3 global smartphone shipments -20% YoY (worst Q3 since 2012), mainly due to memory price hikes and shortages, retail prices up ~20% overall; Samsung raised Galaxy S26 prices Oct 1, Apple raised iPhone 18 Pro prices - memory costs passed through.

Japanese photoresist giants (JSR / Tokyo Ohka / Shin-Etsu) raised all categories a base +15% from Oct 1, spot lots up to +38% (Sina Finance, citing Oct 12); ASML notified Korean customers of a blanket +10% on lithography replacement parts effective for 2027-January deliveries (The Elec via Sina Finance, Oct 10) - fab cost pressure continues to transmit into foundry/OSAT.

Busan Xi-Trump deal (Oct 30): US tariffs on China 57%->47% (fentanyl-related rate down to 10%), China suspends this month's rare-earth export controls for one year and resumes soybean purchases, both sides agree to halt reciprocal port-fee measures; announced publicly by the leaders, implementation details pending. If implemented it would ease cross-border costs for electronic materials.

supplier_updates.detail: R32 holds near historic highs: East China mainstream RMB 63,500-64,500/ton, Dongyue Lv Leng / Juhua quotes RMB 65,500/ton (Oct 14), industry annualized quota utilization 96.71%; R410A RMB 57,000-59,500/ton; R22 ex-factory RMB 19,500/ton (pulled back on softer demand, Oct 21).

LME 3-month copper closed Oct 28 at US$14,484/ton, rebounding ~2.8% from the Oct 22 five-week low of US$14,089 (calculated from observed prices), still below the Oct 12 peak of US$14,657.5/ton; spot silver Oct 29 ~US$52.08-52.38/oz (down ~3.5% on the day).

Nucor Oct 19 customer letter: HRC CSP up another US$15/short ton to US$1,255/short ton (JV CSI to US$1,320), after US$10 to US$1,230 on Oct 5 - consecutive weekly hikes, delivery 3-5 weeks, US HRC +52% YoY (four-year high); domestic HRC soft (Xuzhou Shagang commodity coil RMB 3,390/ton on Oct 27, -RMB 20).

LME 3-month aluminum rebounded to US$3,064/ton on Oct 27 (+1.22%); Wood Mackenzie (Oct 22): ~900Kt-1,000Kt global primary aluminum deficit in 2026 (damaged Middle East smelters took ~2% of capacity offline), swinging to surplus in 2027.

onsemi's second broad price hike effective Oct 10 (channel sources: MOSFET/IGBT/SiC +5%-15%, second this year), TI and Renesas following (Renesas next round 2027-1-1), ST raised prices three times this year (Apr 1 / Jun 28 / Aug 23), Infineon at least twice; mainstream power-device lead times stretched from 8-12 weeks to 30+ weeks; domestic IDMs (China Resources Micro / Silan) +15%+ across the board from Jul 1.

INVT's official price-adjustment letter (issued Sep 7) effective Oct 8: low-voltage drives full range +3%-15%, medium/high-voltage +5%, elevator drives +5%, servo systems (drives + motors) +3%-5%; mainstream brands (ABB / Siemens / Danfoss / Schneider) drive lead times 10-26 weeks and rising (third-party roundup).

Systematic repricing of industrial-control components: Omron / Schneider relays +10%-25%, Turck / Pepperl+Fuchs sensors +15%-35%, Phoenix Contact / Weidmueller connectors +12%-30% (channel compilation); no new breaker/contactor hike letters from Schneider / ABB / Siemens / Chint / Delixi this round; Siemens DI China price adjustment effective 11-01 (2 days to go).

Hitachi Energy announced a C$479 million investment in a transformer insulation material (pressboard) plant in London, Ontario (Canada's first and the largest of its kind globally, online 2028, 20Kt/year pressboard), plus C$270 million to expand large-transformer capacity in Varennes, Quebec (Oct 16); China transformer exports RMB 64.6 billion (+36%, +182% to the US, citing CSC Financial research); North America transformer lead times 128-144 weeks.

Oct 27 praseodymium-neodymium metal down RMB 5,000 to RMB 890,000/ton, praseodymium-neodymium oxide RMB 717,500/ton; West China Securities (Oct 17): light rare earths steady at highs, heavy rare earths (terbium oxide -2.60% WoW) still falling; the Busan deal's one-year pause on rare-earth export controls (leaders announced, details pending) gives NdFeB supply brief breathing room.

Kingboard Laminates raised 2116 and thinner styles and PP another 15% on Oct 13 (multiple rounds this year); Shengyi Technology raised boards/PP another 10%-20% in early October; copper foil tolling: 18-micron HTE RMB 26,000->26,500/ton (steady after Oct 26, Mysteel), Kingboard HTE tolling ~RMB 30,000/ton (~RMB 15,000 a year ago); electronic cloth 7628 lead times 12-18 months.

SK Hynix Oct 28 Q3 call: Q3 DRAM ASP +high-20% QoQ, DDR4 8Gb ~US$26 (~US$6.3 a year ago, ~4x), NAND 128Gb US$30.61 (8x in a year), shortage expected through 2030; Samsung Oct 29: Q3 DRAM ASP +20% QoQ, HBM4 shipments more than tripled QoQ, 2027 HBM capacity fully sold out; TrendForce: Q4 conventional DRAM contract prices +10%-15%, NAND +15%-20%.

Select Samsung Electro-Mechanics MLCC lead times stretched from 39-49 weeks to 61 weeks (DigiKey pricing, new orders deliver end-2027), 47uF high-cap MLCC US$17.50->US$21.60 per 100 pcs Aug-Oct (+23%); TrendForce Oct 29: AI-grade MLCC shortage extends into H1 2027, Murata new capacity unlikely before 2028, Japanese MLCC makers highly likely to follow in November price talks; Murata issued EOL on select part numbers in 9 series in Sep-Oct (last order 2028-3-31); Yageo plans another round late Oct-Nov (high-cap +50%, mid/low-cap +10%-30%), Sanhuan +10%-30% to distributors from October.

Fenghua resistor new-order scheduling 16-20 weeks; general thick-film resistors +15%-20%, alloy resistors +20%-30%; Yageo / Walsin raised prices multiple times this year, capacity sold out (channel/media roundup).

Allegro's third price adjustment Oct 1, China Resources Micro / Silan +15% from July, Renesas has announced the next round for 2027-1-1, Nations Technologies MCU +10%-20% from Oct 1 (official notice); mainstream power-chip lead times 30+ weeks, 8-inch analog devices 20-40 weeks.

Sensor makers ST / Allegro / Novosense / SmartSens +10%-50% (automotive-grade oxygen sensors, industrial Pt100/Pt1000 RTDs, force sensors, channel compilation); automotive MEMS wafer foundry lead times stretched to 36 weeks.

High-speed fiber connectors (CCS / Amphenol) ~50-week lead times (hyperscalers locked in capacity years ahead); Amphenol 10-14 weeks, TE 10-16 weeks (channel survey); Nexans: global cable capacity tight, a new XLPE line takes ~3 years.

Prysmian North America announced utility cable products +5%-7% from Nov 1 (citing continued sharp rises in key raw-material costs); Section 338 on Canada effective Oct 30: some refrigeration equipment removed from the 50% tariff list (some valves added back).

Batch 12 (Cameras-Video, Filter Drier Valves, Gears, Large Motors 100HP+, Packaging: Returnables, Sealed Lead Acid Battery, Test And Drain Valves, Uncategorized Pumps, heat exchangers & cold plates, power devices): no anomalies in 10 categories; 1 substantive hit in Coolants (see below).
subcategories: Large Motors (100 HP And Above 75KW) - Non-Hermetic

supplier_updates.detail: Ethylene glycol purchase prices +20.75% YoY (Tongyi's Q1-Q3 2026 key operating data announcement, Oct 28, primary disclosure), base oil +20.28% YoY, while its antifreeze selling prices -1.05% YoY; ethylene glycol front-month futures up over 5% at the Oct 28 close (RMB 5,276/ton).

No price-hike / shortage / capacity-move news in the last 3 days for Highly, Lingda, GMCC, Danfoss or any compressor type (centrifugal / reciprocating / rotary / scroll / screw); only industry research updates.
No price or lead-time moves for HVAC ECM / fan / pump (Winday's Oct 16 research call covered wind turbines, a different scope from HVAC).
Domestic GCr15 bearing-steel ex-factory prices steady Oct 26-28; no price-hike letters from SKF or other bearing makers.
Only company news such as Sanhua's four-way-valve patent grant (Oct 23) and DunAn Environmental's stop-valve patent grant (Oct 27); no valve price-hike / shortage news.
Stainless heat-exchange tube prices unchanged on Oct 26/27; no price-hike news for HVAC microchannel / finned-tube / shell-and-tube heat exchangers.
Market rumor of AMD FPGA +10%-20% on Dec 27 marked unconfirmed (discarded as Grade C); no crystal-maker price-adjustment letters.

No new price-hike letters from the contract-manufacturing side (the "PCBA price-hike letter" on ipcb.com is a 2021 article, discarded as Grade C); PCB board price hikes are transmitting into contract manufacturing.
